extracted.intended_audience: Toastmasters contest chairs, chief judges, voting/tiebreaking judges, timers, counters, contestants, and other contest officials
extracted.subtask_description: Official rulebook and judging standards governing the conduct, eligibility, judging, timing, scoring, and administration of Toastmasters speech contests (International, Evaluation, Humorous, Table Topics, Tall Tales, Online, and Video) for club through international levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official contest types and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Toastmasters International recognizes and supports the following official speech contests: International Speech Contest, Evaluation Contest, Humorous Speech Contest, Table Topics Contest, Tall Tales Contest, Online Speech Contest, and Video Speech Contest (only for members of undistricted clubs, including Provisional Districts). No other contest types, showcases, etc., can be conducted by Districts (including Areas and Divisions) and Provisional Districts (including Areas and Divisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Districts must conduct the International Speech Contest (in English). Districts may conduct up to three additional English contests and up to four non-English contests (non-English contests must follow corresponding English contest rules and not proceed beyond District level). Modifications to the rulebook only via administrative Protocol. Exceptions are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest progression and origination
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests must originate at the club level and proceed through the Area, Division, and District levels, respectively. Only contests following this progression are permitted at the Area, Division, and District levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Speech Contest is the only contest that proceeds beyond District level to quarterfinals, semifinals, and the World Championship. Provisional Districts follow the same progression (exception: Video Speech Contest). Rules for runoffs when many Divisions exist and rules for replacing winners who cannot advance are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to compete
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to compete in any official Toastmasters speech contest, a member must: 1) Be a paid member of a club in the Area, Division, and District in which they are competing; and 2) Maintain eligibility at all levels of any contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club must be in good standing; new/dual/reinstated members must have dues and application current with World Headquarters. If a contestant is later found ineligible at any prior level, they must be disqualified even if corrected later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional eligibility for International Speech Contest
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to compete in the International Speech Contest, a member must: have earned certificates of completion in Levels 1 and 2 of any path in Pathways or earned a Distinguished Toastmaster award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: charter members of clubs chartered less than one year before the club contest may compete without completing this requirement (club must have chartered before Area contest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible persons to compete
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists categories ineligible to compete in any Toastmasters speech contest (e.g., incumbent International Officers/Directors, Region Advisors/applicants, certain District officers, International officer candidates, Immediate Past District Directors, candidates for upcoming District positions, winners of World Championship/Video Speech Contest as specified, contest officials in certain roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: members serving as voting/tiebreaking/chief judges, timers, counters, presenter/contest chair/toastmaster/event committee chair for the same contest type are ineligible. Members may compete in each club where they hold paid membership but cannot compete in more than one Area contest of a given type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest officials' eligibility (judges/chief judge)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a chief judge, voting judge, or tiebreaking judge: at club level be a paid member; at Area/Division/District be a paid member ≥6 months and have completed min. six speech projects in Competent Communication manual or earned Levels 1 and 2 certificates in Pathways; be physically present at the contest (exceptions for Online).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For International quarterfinals/semifinals/world levels, additional requirements apply (e.g., Advanced Toastmaster/Communicator Bronze or completed at least one Pathways path, prior judging experience at Area/Division/District/semi level). All judges must sign Judge’s Certification of Eligibility and Code of Ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must create their own speeches, and each must be substantially original. Twenty-five percent or less of the speech may be devoted to quoting, paraphrasing, or referencing another person’s content. Any quoted, paraphrased, or referenced content must be so identified during the speech presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before contests, contestants must certify in writing to the chief judge that the content is or will be substantially original using the Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality (Item 1183). If a contestant references another contestant or a speech presented by another contestant at the same contest, that is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech subject selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject of all International, Humorous, Tall Tales, and Online contest speeches must be selected by the contestant. The subject of Table Topics Contest speeches must be determined by the contest chair. Evaluation Contest speeches are limited to oral evaluations of the test speaker’s speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speeches must be delivered from the designated platform/area; contestants and officials must be advised of the speaking area before the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for physical presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each contestant must be physically present to compete beyond the club level. Participation by audio, video, or other remote technology is not permitted beyond the club level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: International Speech Contest Quarterfinals, Online Speech Contest, and Video Speech Contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest staffing and minimum officials by level
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies required contest officials and number of voting judges/timers/counters at each level (e.g., club: contest chair, chief judge, at least five voting judges, tiebreaking judge, two counters, two timers; Area: equal number of voting judges from each club or min five; Division: equal number from each Area or min seven; District: equal number from each Division or min seven with three counters; quarterfinals: min nine voting judges, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting judges must remain anonymous when practical. Chief judge, voting judges, and tiebreaking judge must not be a member of any club with a contestant at certain levels. Online contests require backup timer(s). Officials must not serve in more than one role for same contest at higher levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges’ anonymity and conflict-of-interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting judges at all levels must remain anonymous when practical. The chief judge, voting judge, or tiebreaking judge must not be a member of any club in which a contestant is a member at certain levels. Judges must have no conflict of interest with contestants that would cause bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges must sign the Judge’s Certification of Eligibility and Code of Ethics. The tiebreaking judge’s identity is secret and they do not attend the judges’ briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' Code of Ethics (objectivity and non-discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: I will demonstrate the utmost objectivity by consciously avoiding bias of any kind in selecting first, second, and third place contestants. I will not consider any contestant’s club, Area, Division, District, or region affiliation. I will not consider any contestant’s age, race, color, creed, gender, gender identity, gender expression, national or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, or physical or mental disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: support contest rules and judging standards, refrain from public criticism, only reveal participation and selected scores per rules. At Division/District levels, judges will not be members of same club as any contestant. Judges must not time speeches or consider undertime/overtime when judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges must not time speeches
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will not time the speeches and will not consider the possibility of undertime or overtime when judging a contestant’s speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers are responsible for official timing and any time disqualification decisions; judges must judge content/performance only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefings, drawing speaking order, and contestant arrival protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the contest, contestants are briefed on rules by the contest chair. Contestants will then draw for their speaking position with the contest chair. If a contestant is absent from the briefing, the alternate may attend in their place. If a primary contestant is not present when the person conducting the contest is introduced, the primary contestant is disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If primary contestant arrives after briefing but before person conducting contest is introduced, they may compete if they report to contest chair, have paperwork in order, and waive briefing opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot completion, signature, and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a ballot to be valid, judges shall: complete their ballots by entering their choices for first, second, and third place; sign and print their names on the ballot. E-signatures are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting judges discreetly provide the bottom portion of the ballot to ballot counters (top portion is discarded by judge). Tiebreaking judge provides bottom portion to chief judge; top portion discarded. If votes are not cast for first/second/third, ballot will be voided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabulation and scoring system (3-2-1 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Counter’s Tally Sheet, each contestant receives points: three (3) points for each first-place ranking; two (2) points for each second-place ranking; one (1) point for each third-place ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballot counters compute totals, verify point totals among themselves, rank contestants by points. In event of tie, consult tiebreaking judge's ballot: the tied contestant with highest ranking on tiebreaking ballot gains the place. Counters check Timer’s Report and strike names of contestants disqualified for under/over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiebreaking judge procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity of the tiebreaking judge is secret and known only to the chief judge. The tiebreaking judge does not attend judges’ briefing. Chief judge provides Tiebreaking Judge’s Guide and Ballot prior to contest. In counting room, in event of tie, the chief judge consults the tiebreaking judge’s ballot; the tied contestant who received the highest ranking on the tiebreaking judge’s ballot will gain the contested place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tiebreaking judge must rank all contestants. Separate tiebreaking guides/ballots exist per contest type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement and results protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest chair announces winners after contestant interviews. In contests with three or more participants, announce third, second, then first in reverse order. Winners must be announced prior to end of the event. For some higher rounds (quarterfinals/semifinals) advancing contestants may be announced in no particular order and placement not announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If winners are announced incorrectly, chief judge/counters/timers may immediately interrupt to correct the error. After winners announced, chief judge destroys ballots, time record, and tally sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing responsibilities and signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Two timers appointed: one with stopwatch (maintains official written Time Record Sheet) and one with signaling device (green/yellow/red) in full view of each contestant. Timers follow specified signal times and record official elapsed times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must ensure contestants can view accurate signals. Time Record Sheet is official time and provided to chief judge. For Online Speech Contest, backup timer(s) required in case of technical difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing windows and disqualification thresholds by contest type
rubrics_metrics.description: All speeches must conform to timing guidelines. Examples: International/Humorous/Online = 5–7 minutes; disqualified if <4:30 or >7:30. Table Topics = 1–2 minutes; disqualified if <1:00 or >2:30. Evaluation = 2–3 minutes; disqualified if <1:30 or >3:30. Tall Tales = 3–5 minutes; disqualified if <2:30 or >5:30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal timing specifics given (when green/yellow/red appear and durations). Timers must not consider fractions of a second. If disqualified for time, counters strike names from results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment, lectern, and amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: A lectern/podium will be available but use is optional (exception: Online contestants responsible for their own equipment). If amplification necessary, a fixed-mounted lectern microphone and a portable microphone must be available. All equipment must be available for contestants to practice with prior to the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants are responsible for arranging their preferred setup in a quiet manner before being introduced. Online contest participants responsible for equipment they will use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot handling confidentiality and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: When voting judges finish marking ballots they must discreetly provide the bottom portion to ballot counters (top portion discarded). Tiebreaking judge provides bottom portion to chief judge. Once results tabulated and verified, Notification of Contest Winner and Results Form completed and submitted. All ballots and tally sheet kept by chief judge until after winners announced, then destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide envelopes for ballots/time records if physical. Ballots/tallies are confidential and not to be made available as general information; chief judge retains until destruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for contests with limited participants or single contestant
rubrics_metrics.description: In contests with only one contestant, a contest must still be held, and the contestant must be disqualified if they do not meet timing, originality, and eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for contests with fewer than three participants: announce second (if applicable) and first; winners announced in reverse order. If decision to allow two contestants to advance from club to Area (or Area to Division etc.) must be communicated and applied consistently within District.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality certification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the contest, every contestant must certify in writing to the chief judge that the content of their speech is or will be substantially original using the Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality (Item 1183).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Speaker's Certification form includes eligibility and an Originality section where the contestant certifies compliance and lists contest type, level, speech title, and signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Contest judging items and scoring (Analytical Quality, Recommendations, Technique, Summation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation Contest Judging Items: Analytical Quality (Clear, Focused) — suggested value 40 points; Recommendations (Positive, Specific, Helpful) — suggested 30 points; Technique (Sympathetic, Sensitive, Motivational) — suggested 15 points; Summation (Concise, Encouraging) — suggested 15 points. Total score 100 points possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge’s Guide explains each item: Analytical Quality = analyze strengths/weaknesses clearly and logically; Recommendations = practical, helpful, positive; Technique = manner of presentation, sensitivity; Summation = brief summary and positive close. Ballot requires votes for 1st/2nd/3rd or void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter’s Tally Sheet instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: From each ballot collected, enter 3 points for FIRST place, 2 points for SECOND place, 1 point for THIRD place. After all ballots entered compute totals. Check the Timer’s Report: if any contestants were disqualified by chief judge for speaking under-time or overtime, strike their names from results. If a tie results, refer to the Tiebreaking Judge’s Ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once totals are verified by ballot counters, enter winners (1st/2nd/3rd) and submit names to chair. The balance of tally information is confidential.
